content:
According to the latest report from Bloomberg, Apple is developing a screenless health and fitness tracker to compete with Whoop. The company is reportedly "working on prototypes," but has yet to decide whether to ultimately launch the product.

Bloomberg reports that this internally developed prototype uses a "slim fabric strap with a built-in computing module containing sensors." The project is currently in the "technology exploration" stage, and Bloomberg notes that the product will not be launched until 2028 at the earliest, provided Apple ultimately decides to bring it to market.

The project is said to have the support of Apple's senior executives, including Eddy Cue and Tim Cook. Cue took over Apple's health team last October, replacing the departing Jeff Williams.

Products such as Whoop and Oura Ring are popular among users who do not want to wear a smartwatch but still want to track their health and fitness. According to Reuters, Oura is preparing to go public and recently reported that 3.6 million Oura Rings were sold in the 12 months ending 30 June. Revenue in the nine months ending 30 June grew 74% year over year, reaching US$1.21 billion.

However, Apple remains the leader in the smartwatch market. Apple Watch also offers a much richer set of features than health-and-fitness-focused wearables like Oura and Whoop.
